A year in a dictionary

Source: R/year.R
weft_year.Rd

A year entry of a dictionary is a weft_year: an integer with a class, so that it keeps its place through c(), [, [[, rev(), sort(), unique(), min(), max(), range() and seq(), and year + n and year - n are years. year - year and every other arithmetic give a plain number, and a comparison works as it does on integers. as.integer(), as.numeric(), format() and print() show the bare integer. Every number and wording class (.num, .ord, .and, .range and the rest) prints a year with no thousands mark.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
c(...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
x[...]

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
x[[...]]

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
rev(x)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
sort(x, decreasing = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
unique(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
seq(from, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
Ops(e1, e2)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
Math(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_year'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

...

Further arguments, passed on.

x, e1, e2, from

A weft_year, or a value to combine with one.

decreasing

Whether to sort downwards.

incomparables

Not used.

na.rm

Whether to drop missing values.

Value

A weft_year, or a plain number where the text says so.

Details

When the vctrs package is loaded, a year combined with an integer or a double gives a plain integer or double, and a year with a year gives a year.
